case: bank-025 — La Crosse County Public Safety Communications, Wisconsin — Aurelian voice agent 'Ava' on the non-emergency line
showrunner_ruling_on_the_hard_gate: COST HOLDS. TIMELINE ACCEPTED NARROWLY, and the email says so. The decision-to-contract interval could not be established from any source; the county web estate returned 403 to every request and its meeting PDFs are not full-text indexed. What survived is La Crosse-specific and sourced: the county's own announcement that the platform underwent several months of intensive training before implementation (c18), paired with a firm go-live of May 5 2025 (c01). Dana's actual question is 'roughly how long before it worked', and that answers it. The deck states it exactly as scoped and never as a decision-to-working interval. Spokane's six weeks is OFF LIMITS under any framing because it is a different vendor entirely.

analysis.label: analysis
analysis.statement: The build sits at rung 4 on the feasibility ladder. Every step was drawn by a person at build time: answer the non-emergency line (c22), classify the intent, collect the location (c23), forward or text (c24), escalate on a keyword match (c25), hand to a human on request (c26). Nothing on any fetched page shows the system choosing its own path or its own tools. The biweekly vendor meeting (c28) is the human owning the loop.
analysis.why_not_a_claim: The rung assignment is our judgement applied to verified mechanism facts, not something any source states.
analysis.how_it_may_be_used: THE CURRICULUM PAYLOAD, and a friendly correction rather than a dunk. The vendor and the press both call it an agent. Rung 4 is the right answer for this job, and saying so plainly teaches Dana the distinction they will use in their next demo.

analysis.label: analysis
analysis.statement: Containment is not resolution. The county's 65 percent (c04) counts calls that ended without a dispatcher answering. A call where the caller hung up confused counts the same as a call where the caller got exactly what they needed. The vendor's 67 percent (c40) uses the stronger verb 'resolving' for what is measured the same way: absence of a transfer.
analysis.why_not_a_claim: Our reading of what the two numbers measure, not a statement either source makes.
analysis.how_it_may_be_used: Say it in the same breath as the number, in ONE sentence, and move on. It is the single most useful thing Dana can carry into a vendor meeting, and it belongs inside the sentence, not on its own slide.

analysis.label: analysis
analysis.statement: Usage-based pricing means the bill rises as the thing works. Year one about $67,000, year two about $81,000, priced on call volume (c10, c11, c14).
analysis.why_not_a_claim: Any percentage increase is our arithmetic on two rounded, approximate figures. Do not print a percentage.
analysis.how_it_may_be_used: Print the two dollar figures and the words 'priced on call volume'. Let Dana do the arithmetic. For a seasonal Anchorage operator this is the most transferable warning in the case: model your July, not your February.

analysis.label: analysis
analysis.statement: This is capacity, not cash. The county's administrator said explicitly that the change would not affect staffing levels and was about creating more capacity (c36). No page fetched today names a deferred hire, cut overtime, or reduced contractor spend.
analysis.why_not_a_claim: The conclusion is ours; the quote is the fact.
analysis.how_it_may_be_used: The deck must NOT convert freed dispatcher time into dollars. Name the decision that was NOT made, because that is the honest and more interesting version: they spent about one salary to stop paying four trained emergency dispatchers per shift to answer parking questions, and they kept all four.

analysis.label: analysis
analysis.statement: The entity to describe on slide 2 is the dispatch center, not the county. The county headcount could not be independently established (c51), but the center's shape is well documented: at least four dispatchers per shift (c37), authorised for 28 seats with 22 filled per the vendor (c38), open 24/7, taking roughly 105,000 non-emergency calls a year (c08).
analysis.why_not_a_claim: A directing recommendation, not a fact.
analysis.how_it_may_be_used: LEAD WITH THE DESK, NOT THE EMPLOYER. A 24/7 phone line with four people on it that became the default number for everything is a shape Dana recognises instantly. A county government is a shape Dana files under 'not me'.

1_size_and_not_tech.detail: Not a technology company: HOLDS, unambiguously. Employee band: WEAU reported March 2026 that the county 'currently has over 200 employees' (c51), inside the band, but uncorroborated; the county web estate returned 403 on every attempt and the ACFR PDF could not be text-extracted. The unit the deck describes is the DISPATCH CENTER: at least four dispatchers per shift (independent, c37) and 28 authorised seats with 22 filled (vendor, c38).

2_one_named_bottleneck.detail: Strongest element in the case. c31, c32, c33, c34, in the operator's own words.

3_bought_not_built.detail: Cleanest buy-not-build in the bank. Bought a named vendor's voice agent (c02), pointed at one line (c22, c27). No engineers, no platform, no custom code on any fetched page.

4_measurable_before_and_after.detail: A real baseline and a real after number, with two caveats that must ride with them. Three fetched pages give three different accounts of the 2024 split (c06-c09), so the baseline is rough, not audited. And the after number is CONTAINMENT, not resolution, with no resolution, satisfaction, callback or complaint figure anywhere (c53). Survives scoped honestly. Does not survive being presented as clean.

5_cost_and_timeline_HARD_GATE.detail: COST: HOLDS, and it is the best-documented cost in the bank. Two independent outlets on La Crosse (c10, c11, c13), a same-product second agency (c15), a same-product third agency's contract terms (c16), and the pricing basis named (c14). TIMELINE: the decision-to-contract date could NOT be established from any source. What survived is La Crosse-specific and sourced: several months of intensive training before implementation (c18) paired with a firm go-live of May 5 2025 (c01). SHOWRUNNER RULING: accepted narrowly, because Dana's actual question is 'roughly how long before it worked' and that answers it. Flagged in the email as the run's one soft edge.

6_named_human_on_record.detail: Cory Lynch, operations supervisor, title confirmed identically across three independent outlets (c30), quoted verbatim in five. Plus David Steinberg, public safety communications administrator (c36), and Sheriff Christy Knowles at Ozaukee (c44-c48).

7_recency.detail: Go-live May 2025, results reported December 2025, follow-up coverage April and May 2026. The most recent case this series has shipped.

viability_note: SHIP IT, with the corrections above and one hard scoping rule. Eleven pages fetched across nine independent outlets plus the vendor's own case study, five named humans on the record, a cost disclosed twice for this agency and twice more for peer agencies, a mechanism confirmed sentence by sentence, and a same-product public failure at a neighbouring county that gives the limit beat teeth no vendor page could. Nothing died that the case depends on. THE HARD SCOPING RULE: the 65 percent is a share of the 41,000 calls the system took, not of the county's 105,000 annual non-emergency calls, and it counts calls that ended, not calls that got answered. Any slide that multiplies 65 percent by 105,000, or implies two thirds of the county's nuisance calls are gone, makes a claim no source supports. Written honestly the number is still excellent: a phone desk with four people on it took 41,000 calls off its own hands in seven months for about the price of one hire, and the county says it did not cut a single position.
